- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce forecast peaks when sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment; model should adjust downward more aggressively when sentiment is consistently negative.
- Lagged price movements often overshoot in forecasts — model should smooth out recent trend continuation and reduce momentum bias.
- Mean reversion is stronger in high volatility periods — forecasts should be adjusted toward historical mean if sentiment is weak or sentiment shifts from positive to neutral.
- When sentiment is positive but price is falling, model should not assume continuation — reduce forecast slope to avoid “sentiment-driven overcorrection.”
- Forecast horizon 30d tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings — apply dampening factor for sentiment volatility > 0.3 in recent 5 days.
